tests.name: Runtime availability
tests.question: Can Infrastry start the application and keep its process reachable?
tests.nextTest: Deploy the unchanged harness on one more fresh runtime instance.

tests.name: Dynamic port routing
tests.question: Does Infrastry supply and route the application port correctly?
tests.nextTest: Repeat on a fresh runtime and confirm the platform-supplied port remains reachable.

tests.name: Environment injection
tests.question: Do configured environment values reach the running application?
tests.nextTest: Repeat on a fresh deployment without editing the configured sentinel.

tests.name: Default runtime filesystem write
tests.question: Is the configured DATA_DIR writable without an explicit Infrastry Volume mounted there?
tests.nextTest: Test an explicit Infrastry Volume separately before drawing any conclusion about persistent storage support.

tests.name: Application storage model
tests.question: Does application filesystem identity persist across independent runtime replacements when a writable identity exists?
tests.nextTest: Mount an explicit volume or obtain a writable runtime path, then replace the runtime and compare identity.

tests.name: Managed database connection
tests.question: Can the application connect to the managed PostgreSQL dependency?
tests.nextTest: Repeat on a fresh runtime using the existing managed database.

tests.name: Managed database persistence
tests.question: Does PostgreSQL preserve identity and existing data across application replacement?
tests.nextTest: Replace the application runtime again and compare database identity, endpoint fingerprint, row count and boot history.

tests.name: Process replacement continuity
tests.question: Can a new application process become healthy while durable dependencies remain available?
tests.nextTest: Perform another no-behavior-change deployment and verify the new instance becomes healthy.

tests.name: Graceful shutdown
tests.question: Does application replacement produce a durable graceful-shutdown receipt?
tests.nextTest: Perform another controlled deployment and correlate the durable shutdown receipt with Infrastry Runtime/Platform logs.

tests.name: HTTPS proxy
tests.question: Does the public proxy deliver HTTPS correctly to the application?
tests.nextTest: Verify HTTPS again from a fresh runtime instance.

tests.name: WebSocket proxy
tests.question: Do WebSocket upgrades and echo traffic survive the public proxy?
tests.nextTest: Run the Safe Automated Suite on a fresh runtime instance.

tests.name: Readiness/liveness separation
tests.question: Can the harness hold liveness at HTTP 200 while readiness returns HTTP 503?
tests.nextTest: Run the automated 60-second readiness test with a new correlation ID.

tests.name: Platform readiness response
tests.question: How does Infrastry react when the app stays alive but reports not-ready?
tests.nextTest: Run the 60-second readiness test, inspect Infrastry monitoring/logs, then record the observed platform response.

tests.name: Runtime log capture
tests.question: Are correlated stdout and stderr markers captured accurately in Application Logs?
tests.nextTest: Run the Safe Automated Suite, find its Runtime correlation ID in Application Logs, then confirm it once.

tests.name: Access logging
tests.question: Are controlled HTTP 200/404/500 responses visible and attributable in Access logs?
tests.nextTest: Run the Safe Automated Suite and verify its 200/404/500 correlation IDs in Access logs.

tests.name: Crash recovery
tests.question: Does Infrastry detect and recover from an intentional application process exit?
tests.nextTest: Enable the protected chaos control, trigger one intentional exit and measure recovery without stressing the platform.

tests.name: Secret redaction
tests.question: Are controlled secret-shaped values masked in developer-facing logs?
tests.nextTest: Use a dedicated synthetic secret probe; never emit a real credential.

tests.name: Failed release isolation
tests.question: Does a failed candidate release leave the previously healthy release available?
tests.nextTest: Use a deliberately non-launching test revision and verify the prior release remains available.

tests.name: Runtime version pinning
tests.question: Does Infrastry honor an exact supported Node.js version request?
tests.nextTest: Pin an exact supported Node version in a controlled revision and compare the running version.

tests.name: Database migration safety
tests.question: Can a backwards-compatible schema migration deploy without losing existing data?
tests.nextTest: Apply a reversible additive schema migration and verify old rows plus new schema after deployment.

tests.name: Rollback continuity
tests.question: Can an earlier application revision be restored without losing durable database state?
tests.nextTest: If Infrastry exposes rollback, restore a known prior revision and verify application plus database continuity.
